newsitem.title: JAPAN: Beheading murder case sent to Japan family court.
newsitem.headline: Beheading murder case sent to Japan family court.

text.p: A 15-year-old boy accused of strangling and beheading an 11-year-old playmate was transferred on Friday to a local family court, which said its proceedings would not be made public.
In a formal document of accusation, the Kobe District Prosecutors' Office said that the boy, whose name was withheld because he is a minor, was suspected of choking Jun Hase to death on May 24.
On the following day, the boy decapitated the body and placed the severed head at the gate of the junior high school both attended in the western port city of Kobe, the prosecutors said.
A note stuck in Hase's mouth said the murderer was taking revenge on Japan's rigid education system.
After the suspect's transfer on Friday, the family court placed him in a juvenile detention centre.
A spokesman for the Kobe Family Court said the court proceedings would be closed to the public.
The boy is also accused of killing a 10-year-old girl and attacking three teenage girls.
Under Japanese law if the boy is found guilty of the murders he will face a maxiumum sentence of three years detention at a juvenile correction centre.

Media reports have said the boy has confessed to all the attacks and showed police a pond where he disposed of a hammer, a knife and a saw used to decapitate Hase. The weapons have all been recovered by police divers.
The reports said the boy, who had a history of beheading cats and pigeons, stole the weapons from shops so they could not be traced to him.
